It also induces autophagic markers (LC3-I to LC3-II conversion, vacuolation) in glioma cells, consistent with suppression of mTOR-driven anabolic signaling and activation of autophagy.

Separately, PI-103 potently drives nuclear FOXO3 translocation via combined mTORC1/mTORC2 inhibition, more effectively than rapamycin or PI3K-selective inhibitors (PMID 36080182). These are direct cell-based mechanistic data consistent with modulation of mTOR/nutrient-sensing signaling, but all studies are in cancer cell lines (glioma, leukemia stem cells, orbital preadipocytes) studying disease-specific endpoints, not aging biomarkers.

No long-term or normal-tissue toxicity/aging-relevant safety data are provided.
